title: Activists breach Microsoft data centre site in Amsterdam

tea.why: Activists oppose the construction of a large Microsoft data centre in Amsterdam due to its massive energy use and environmental impact.
tea.want: They demand an immediate stop to the construction of the data centre project.
tea.changed: Nov 6: Protesters broke through fences, climbed a crane and roof at the construction site, leading to police interventions and arrests.

summary: Activists gathered and breached the fences of a Microsoft data centre construction site in the Sloterdijk area of Amsterdam. The demonstration, part of broader European actions against data centres, was organised by groups including Geef Tegengas and Fossielvrij NL. Protesters opposed the facility over its high electricity consumption, which they say equals all Amsterdam households combined and stalls the building of new homes, as well as alleged links between Microsoft and the Gaza conflict. Riot police were deployed to the area in large numbers, surrounded parts of the demonstration, and made several arrests after the mayor banned the protest. Microsoft stated it respects peaceful protest rights but condemns illegal and unsafe actions.
demands: Stop construction of the Microsoft data centre
Halt new large data centres over energy grid and housing impacts
response: Police deployed riot units, surrounded demonstrators, and made several arrests after the mayor banned the protest. Microsoft stated it was aware of the incident, respects peaceful expression, but condemns illegal actions that endanger safety.
